review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the helper lemmas against each other. The strongest repetition is the integral-splitting argument for the 13-term bound (`f² + Σ g² + ΣΣ h²` ≤ 13·B). It appears in `vorticityContinuityExport_sliceSobolevBound` and again in `vorticityContinuityExport_limitSliceDerivatives`. The second finding is weaker: the six `≤ |Kw|+|K1|+|K2|` chains are individually short, but they appear six times across two theorems. The `hsq`/`hGsum`/`hHsum` pieces overlap with the first finding. I did not check other files for a ready-made lemma that already does this. Neither proposed lemma has been compiled. Exact `rw` and unification details, such as the `Finset.sum_const` simp for 3·B and 9·B, may need small adjustments.

findings.problem: Two proofs repeat the same argument. For integrable a, b_j, c_jk on a set S, with ∫a ≤ B, ∫b_j ≤ B and ∫c_jk ≤ B, they split ∫(a + Σ_j b_j + Σ_jΣ_k c_jk) with integral_add and integral_finsetSum, then bound the sums by 3·B and 9·B with Finset.sum_le_sum and a constant-sum calc. The first copy is lines 156–176 (S = vec3Ball, integrability from `hib` and continuity). The second is lines 226–266 (S = Bs, integrability from MemLp squares, with hGsum, hHsum, hGsumInt, hHsumInt, hIntSplit). The two copies differ only in how integrability is obtained, so about 40 lines of measure-theoretic bookkeeping are written twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma before `sliceSobolevBound`:
`private theorem vorticityContinuityExport_integral_thirteen_le {S : Set Vec3} (a : Vec3 → ℝ) (b : Fin 3 → Vec3 → ℝ) (c : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Vec3 → ℝ) (B : ℝ) (ha : IntegrableOn a S) (hb : ∀ j, IntegrableOn (b j) S) (hc : ∀ j k, IntegrableOn (c j k) S) (hBa : ∫ x in S, a x ≤ B) (hBb : ∀ j, ∫ x in S, b j x ≤ B) (hBc : ∀ j k, ∫ x in S, c j k x ≤ B) : ∫ x in S, (a x + ∑ j : Fin 3, b j x + ∑ j : Fin 3, ∑ k : Fin 3, c j k x) ≤ 13 * B`.
Proof sketch: integrability of the two sums comes from `integrable_finsetSum`. Then `integral_add` twice and `integral_finsetSum` (for the inner sum too) turn the left side into ∫a + Σ∫b_j + ΣΣ∫c_jk. Finally `Finset.sum_le_sum` gives the bounds 3B and 9B, and `linarith`/`ring` finishes.
Use in `sliceSobolevBound`: after `rw [e]`, `exact vorticityContinuityExport_integral_thirteen_le (fun y => f (y, t) ^ 2) (fun j y => gg j (y, t) ^ 2) (fun j k y => hh j k (y, t) ^ 2) B (hib _ cf) (fun j => hib _ (cg j)) (fun j k => hib _ (ch j k)) hB1 hB2 hB3`.
Use in `limitSliceDerivatives`, after `refine ⟨hfirst, hsecond, ?_⟩`: `exact vorticityContinuityExport_integral_thirteen_le (fun x => ωt x ^ 2) (fun j x => G j x ^ 2) (fun j k x => H j k x ^ 2) A hωsq hGsq hHsq hωbound hGbound hHbound`.
Both call sites should unify up to beta reduction. No new imports are needed, because `integral_add`, `integral_finsetSum` and `integrable_finsetSum` are already in scope.
findings.benefit: The 13 = 1 + 3 + 9 counting and the integrability and splitting bookkeeping live in one place. `hGsum`, `hHsum`, `hGsumInt`, `hHsumInt`, `hIntSplit`, `h2` and `h3` disappear from both theorems. Each theorem then reads as its analytic content: Sobolev embedding in one, weak-derivative passage to the limit in the other. A change to the constant or the split now needs one edit instead of two.

findings.problem: The budget comparison Kw, K1, K2 ≤ |Kw|+|K1|+|K2| is re-proved six times, each with a different `le_add_of_nonneg_*` chain. The three `henergy` blocks are at lines 341–348, 353–360 and 367–377 in `controlledMollificationIntegrals`. The three `hKw'`/`hK1'`/`hK2'` blocks are at lines 486–510 in `stageTimeSliceLimits`. Each block also repeats the long integral expression. The two theorems use the same pattern, and the duplication invites inconsistent edits.
findings.proposed_change: Add a small lemma `vorticityContinuityExport_le_absSum (Kw K1 K2 : ℝ) : Kw ≤ |Kw| + |K1| + |K2| ∧ K1 ≤ |Kw| + |K1| + |K2| ∧ K2 ≤ |Kw| + |K1| + |K2|`. Prove it with `le_abs_self` plus `abs_nonneg` and `linarith`. In `controlledMollificationIntegrals`, each `henergy` becomes `hKw.trans hle.1`, `(hK1 m).trans hle.2.1` or `(hK2 m k).trans hle.2.2`. In `stageTimeSliceLimits`, `hKw'`, `hK1'` and `hK2'` become the same three one-line terms. This can also absorb `vorticityContinuityExport_energyBound`'s role, since the caller only needs `X ≤ S`. The lemma needs no new imports.
findings.benefit: It removes six hand-built inequality chains and about 40 lines. It also makes explicit that the single budget S = |Kw|+|K1|+|K2| dominates all three stage energies.
